title: Is a Mokoro Trip in the Okavango Right for Your Club? How Canoes, Polers and Island Camps Work for a Group
meta_title: Mokoro Trip in the Okavango: How Groups Pair Up
meta_description: Planning a mokoro trip in the Okavango for a club or group? Canoe pairing, island camps, best months, costs and safety on a Botswana Delta trip.
excerpt: A mokoro trip puts your group two to a canoe in Botswana's Okavango Delta, poled through silent channels to an island camp. Here is how clubs plan one.
content:
A mokoro trip takes you into Botswana's Okavango Delta in a dugout-style canoe, two passengers to each boat with a local poler standing behind them. Groups usually leave from Maun, pole for one to two hours to an island, then camp, walk and paddle there for one or two nights, at water level and in near silence.

Getting a whole club, society or circle of friends into those two-seat canoes takes more planning than booking a couple. This guide covers how pairing, polers and island camps work for a group, which months have the water, honest costs and safety, and how our club and society safaris turn the Delta into a shared trip rather than a seat in a stranger's convoy.

Quick Facts

  • Boat: A mokoro, now usually fibreglass, carries two passengers plus a standing poler
  • Starting point: Maun, with a road transfer to a mokoro station on the Delta's edge
  • Time on the water: Around 1 to 2 hours from the station to an island camp
  • Best months: June to September for high water; July is usually the flood peak
  • Group maths: One canoe and one poler for every two people
  • Fitness: Average: sit still in a low canoe and walk gently on flat ground
  • Health: Ngamiland, which includes the Delta, is a higher-risk malaria area (checked November 2026)

What Is a Mokoro Trip in the Okavango Delta?

A mokoro trip is a guided outing in a narrow canoe pushed through the Okavango's reed channels and lagoons by a poler using a long pole. There is no engine, so you hear frogs, birds and moving animals, and you sit with your eyes just above the waterline.

The traditional mokoro was carved from a single tree trunk. Most boats used for visitors today are fibreglass, which spares the large trees the Delta's communities once had to fell. The way of travelling has not changed: the poler stands at the stern, reads the current and the reeds, and steers between water lilies and papyrus.

What you see from a canoe is different from a game drive. Reed frogs clinging to stems, malachite kingfishers, jacanas walking on lily pads and fish eagles overhead are the everyday sightings. Elephants, lechwe and hippos are often seen across a lagoon or from an island, and your poler keeps a respectful distance from anything large.

Day mokoro trip or overnight island camp?

A day mokoro trip from Maun means a road transfer, a few hours poling and a short walk before driving back. An overnight trip sleeps on an island in a simple bush camp, which gives you the dawn walk and the evening on the water that most people remember. For a group, the overnight version is usually worth it, because so much of a day trip goes on getting there.

How Does a Group Fit Into a Fleet of Two-Seat Canoes?

A group fits by splitting into pairs, one pair per canoe, with a poler for each. Twelve people on a mokoro trip means six mokoros and six polers moving in a loose line, with a lead guide setting the pace and choosing where to stop. Odd numbers are fine: one canoe carries a single passenger or extra kit.

That simple maths shapes the whole trip. The mokoro station needs enough canoes and polers free on your dates, so tell us your final head count early. For larger clubs we often split the group into two flotillas that leave half an hour apart, which keeps channels quiet and wildlife relaxed, then everyone meets at the same island camp.

Pairing people up

Pair a nervous paddler with a calm one, and put keen photographers together so they can agree when to stop. Couples usually share, but a mokoro trip is also a good chance to mix a club that only knows each other from meetings. Swap pairs on day two so everyone spends time with different people and a different poler.

Tents, meals and the island camp

The island camp is simple: dome tents, a campfire, a bush toilet and meals cooked on the fire. On our trip, camping equipment, bed linen and towels are supplied, so the group carries only personal bags. Ask for tent sharing to follow the same logic as the canoes, and flag any single travellers early so they are not squeezed in.

Which Okavango Canoe Trip Style Suits Your Group Best?

The right style depends on budget and how much comfort your group needs. Mokoro camping from Maun is the most affordable and the most adventurous. A water camp inside the Delta includes mokoro outings with proper beds and flights. A longer mobile safari can add a mokoro afternoon to game drives in Moremi and Khwai.

For a full comparison of water camps, land camps and the Delta's concessions, our Okavango Delta safari planning guide goes deeper. If your group is torn between the Delta and the elephant herds on the river further north, read our Okavango Delta vs Chobe comparison first.

When Should a Group Book Its Mokoro Trip?

A group should aim for June to September, when the flood that starts in the Angolan highlands has filled the Delta's seasonal channels. The water usually reaches Botswana around March or April, spreads through May, peaks around July and shrinks again from August into October. For a mokoro trip in those months, book six to twelve months ahead.

MonthsWater and weatherMokoro verdict
December to FebruaryLowest water; hot, with afternoon thunderstormsShort trips in permanent channels only; many routes are dry
March to MayFlood enters the Delta and spreads; rains ease, nights coolRoutes open week by week; May is a good shoulder month
June to AugustHigh water, dry days, cold nights that can fall below 5°CBest time for a mokoro trip; bring warm layers
SeptemberWater still high but receding; warmer daysVery good, with fewer cold mornings
October to NovemberWater shrinking; October often tops 40°C; first rains in NovemberPossible in deeper channels; plan walks early and rest at midday

Every year's flood is different, so we check levels for your dates before confirming. Our best time to visit Botswana guide covers the rest of the country month by month if you are combining regions.

How Much Does a Group Canoe Trip in the Delta Cost?

Our 3-day Okavango Delta mokoro tour starts from USD 715 per adult, covering two nights in an island bush camp, a guide and poler, meals, drinks, transfers from Maun and non-resident park fees. The final group price depends on dates, group size and water conditions.

Group pricing works differently from a couple's booking. Each canoe needs its own poler, so canoe costs grow with head count rather than shrinking, but the transfer vehicle, lead guide and camp crew are shared, which helps larger groups. We quote one clear per-person figure for the whole club, with single tents and optional extras shown separately.

Government fees can also move. In February 2026 Botswana proposed raising the non-resident park entry fee from P380 to P500, according to a Botswana Daily News report on the proposed tourism fees; at the end of July the government said current fees would stay for now while talks continue (checked November 2026). Confirm the latest position before you set a price for members.

Is a Mokoro Trip Safe With Hippos and Crocodiles Around?

A guided mokoro trip is considered safe when the group follows the poler. Polers grow up on these waters and know where hippos rest, which channels are too deep and when to wait. The canoe stays in shallow channels, and the rules are simple: sit still, keep hands and feet inside and talk quietly.

Island walks follow the same logic. The guide walks in front, the group walks in single file behind, and nobody wanders off to take a photo. Brief the club on this before you leave Maun, because a group of friends tends to chat and spread out, which is exactly what a walking guide does not want.

Health and insurance for the mokoro trip

The NHS Fit for Travel page on Botswana lists Ngamiland, which includes the Okavango Delta, among the higher-risk malaria districts, with the highest risk from November to June (checked November 2026). Members should see a travel clinic six to eight weeks before departure. Make sure everyone has cover for remote areas and evacuation; our travel insurance page explains what to look for.

Many nationalities can visit Botswana without a visa. Anyone who needs one can apply through the Botswana government visitor visa page, so check every member's passport early.

How Do You Fit the Delta Into a Longer Botswana Group Safari?

Most groups pair a two-night mokoro trip with three or four days of game drives. The canoe days give quiet and birdlife; the drives deliver lions, wild dogs and big elephant herds. Maun links both, so the mokoro section slots neatly at the start or end of a vehicle safari.

Our 5-day Okavango exploration through Moremi and Khwai already combines game drives, a Moanachira channel boat cruise, a mokoro outing and a night drive, and works well after a mokoro camping trip. Clubs with a camera habit should also read our Botswana photography safari for groups, while riding clubs can add the Delta on horseback with our Okavango horse riding safari guide.

If you are new to running a trip for others, our page on organising a group safari walks through deposits, rooming lists and payment deadlines. You can also browse all our group safaris and the wider range of Botswana safari packages.

Insider Tips

  • Soft bags only: Canoes have no room for hard suitcases; leave big luggage in Maun
  • Dry bags: Put phones, cameras and spare batteries in a dry bag inside your day pack
  • Neutral colours: Khaki, olive and brown blend in on island walks; skip white and bright colours
  • Hat and cover: There is no shade on the water, so bring a wide-brimmed hat, long sleeves and sunscreen
  • Warm layers: June to August dawns are cold on the water; pack a fleece and a hat for evenings
  • Tip the polers: Tips are not included; agree a club kitty in advance so every poler is thanked fairly

Frequently Asked Questions

How many people fit in a mokoro?

A mokoro normally carries two passengers sitting low in the canoe, with a poler standing at the back to push it along. That means a group needs one canoe and one poler for every two people, so a club of 12 travels as a line of six mokoros. Bags for an overnight trip ride in the canoes too.

When is the best time for a mokoro trip in the Okavango?

The best time for a mokoro trip in the Okavango Delta is roughly June to September, when the annual flood from Angola has filled the seasonal channels and the weather is dry. July is usually the peak of the flood. Permanent channels allow shorter trips all year, but December to February brings low water and storms.

Is a mokoro trip safe for a group?

A guided mokoro trip is considered safe when everyone follows the poler's instructions: sit still, keep hands out of the water and stay quiet near animals. Polers read the channels and keep a wide distance from hippos and elephants. The main risks are wildlife, sun and malaria, so a proper briefing, sun cover and antimalarial advice matter.

Do you need to be fit for a mokoro trip?

You do not need to be very fit for a mokoro trip. Passengers sit while the poler does the work, and island walks go at a gentle pace on flat, uneven ground. Anyone who can climb into a low canoe, sit for one to two hours and walk for a couple of hours in the heat will manage.

How long should a group spend on a mokoro trip?

Most groups should plan two nights on a mokoro trip from Maun. A day trip gives a taste, but much of it goes on the drive and the first hour on the water. Two nights on an island allow dawn and evening walks, a poling lesson and a sundowner on the water before you return.

Final Thoughts

A mokoro trip works beautifully for a group once you accept its rhythm: two to a canoe, a poler each, a simple island camp and long, quiet hours on the water. Pick the high-water months, confirm numbers early and pair people with care.
